subject: Technical recap & roadmap: latency budgets, throughput needs, and residency clarifications
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Timothy Blake <timothy@finmed.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Technical recap & roadmap: latency budgets, throughput needs, and residency clarifications

Timothy — thanks for taking the time today. Short recap + requested inputs so we can finalize a targeted pilot proposal.

Key points we captured on the call:
- Latency targets (service-level asks): p50 ~ 40–60ms, p95 <= 120ms for US; EU p95 <= 160–220ms; APAC p95 target closer to 250–350ms depending on region.
- Throughput: expected production baseline ~ 450–600 qps, with predictable daily peaks up to ~1.5k qps for short bursts.
- Streaming: ~200 concurrent streaming sessions at peak; average stream duration 18–30s; token rate ~12–20 tokens/sec.
- Concurrency: expected 6–12 concurrent requests per user session for product flows.
- Data residency: EU PHI must remain in EU-region-hosted instances; US data can route through our US clusters. No cross-border synching of raw request payloads.

Asks / action items for FinMed (would be great to get these by EOD Wed):
1) Sample traffic skeleton (CSV or JSON) showing QPS by hour for a typical weekday and peak day. If you prefer, attach a 24-row CSV with the hourly qps. (Attachment stub in example: finmed_sample_qps.csv)
2) Clarify percent of requests that are streaming vs one-shot (rough ratio).
3) Confirm which data elements are considered PHI and whether payloads will be tokenized/encrypted before sending.
4) Priority regions for pilot (choose one of: US-East, EU-West, APAC-SG) — we recommend starting US+EU for the initial trial.

Next steps from Redwood: Diego will draft a quantified SLO matrix and suggested SLO cushions for burst windows; Kimberly will prepare a short deployment options note that lists dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for residency; I will assemble a short pilot timeline and cost estimate.

Attachments: finmed_sample_qps.csv (placeholder)

Thanks — happy to hop on another quick sync if it helps.

— Olga

From: Timothy Blake <timothy@finmed.com>

Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical recap & roadmap: latency budgets, throughput needs, and residency clarifications

Olga — this looks great, thanks for the structured recap. Quick clarifications from our side: 
- We can export an hourly QPS CSV; attaching a first-pass (see attached). Expect the baseline on weekdays to average ~520 qps with spikes to ~1.6k on limited promotional windows.
- Streaming is roughly 18% of requests today; streaming sessions tend to be a mix of short (10–20s) and medium (30–45s), depending on workflow.
- PHI: the only payload fields labeled PHI are patient name, DOB, and direct identifiers; clinical notes are considered sensitive but encrypted-at-rest. We can token-replace names prior to sending if needed.
- Priority regions: US-East primary, EU-West secondary for pilot. APAC is planned but not in the initial scope.

Cc'd Anna (platform lead) — Anna, can you confirm whether you can remove/replace direct identifiers before sending sample payloads?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Timothy
Timothy Blake
Head of Platform | FinMed Health
Timothy.Blake@finmed.com

Karthik — forwarding FinMed's reply and the sample QPS file. High level asks for SRE/serving runbook perspective (please reply inline or as a short doc):
1) Based on the CSV, what baseline capacity estimate would we provision as hosted vs dedicated to hit p95 targets in US/EU? Assume standard 200-token avg response and 12 tokens/sec streaming rate.
2) For the streaming slice (~18% of requests), what concurrency headroom would we need to guarantee 250ms p95 in US-East? If we can't hit 250ms for streaming, propose target and fallback.
3) Data residency: given they want EU-West to keep PHI in-region, what is the simplest private config (VPC/private-control-plane or dedicated-residency) to ensure no cross-border payload ingress? Rough cost delta preferred.
4) Quick list of telemetry we need from them to validate SLOs during pilot (examples: p99 token latency, streaming setup RTT, backend queue depth, kube pod counts).

Diego/Kimberly — please add any product/ops constraints I'm missing. Happy to triage a follow-up call with FinMed if you want to review together.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Technical recap & roadmap: latency budgets, throughput needs, and residency clarifications

Thanks — I'll produce the SLO matrix and a short bullets doc by EOD tomorrow. Initial thoughts:
- We should propose a p95 target of 120ms for US-East (non-stream), p95 180ms for EU-West given cross-region network, and a streaming p95 of 200–300ms depending on session size.
- For their 1.6k burst profile, recommend a dual-tier approach: reserved baseline for 600 qps (dedicated on first month) + burst autoscaling pool for the remainder, with a warm fast-path for short queries to reduce cold-starts.
- Residency: propose a private-control-plane configuration for EU PHI (keeps control plane in EU, data-plane pinned to EU GPUs), cheaper than full on-prem and simpler onboarding.

I'll attach the SLO template (requested_slo_template.xlsx) when complete.

— Kim
